The Southern Taurid meteor shower peaks on November 4–5, 2026, but its predicted maximum falls after midnight on November 6 in India. Here's when and where to watch the shower and what makes its bright fireballs special.

The Southern Taurid meteor shower is reaching its main peak in early November, but skywatchers may come across two different dates in 2026. November 4–5 will be peak night for this meteor shower but according to time difference, it will be seen at midnight on November 6 in India. The shower is known for its slow-moving meteors and occasional bright fireballs, offering observers another opportunity to watch the night sky.

November 4, 5 Or 6: At what time is the meteor show?

The International Meteor Organization and American Meteor Society list November 4–5 as the peak night for the Southern Taurids. However, the predicted maximum is around 19:00 UTC on November 5.

For observers in India, this translates to approximately 12:30 am IST on November 6. This difference in time zones explains why November 5 and November 6 both appear in forecasts. The shower is active from September 20 to November 20, giving skywatchers several weeks to observe its meteors.

Southern Taurid Meteor Shower 2026: Bright fireballs but 5 meteors per hour! 

The Southern Taurids are a relatively low-activity meteor shower. Under ideal dark-sky conditions, observers can expect around five meteors per hour.

However, the shower is particularly known for occasional bright fireballs. These are exceptionally luminous meteors that can appear much brighter than ordinary shooting stars.

Southern Taurid Meteor Shower 2026: Why it produces fireballs?

The Southern Taurids originate from debris left behind by Comet 2P/Encke. As Earth passes through this stream of dust and rocky particles, some enter the atmosphere at high speeds and burn up, creating visible streaks of light. The larger particles associated with the Taurid stream can produce particularly bright displays.

Southern Taurid Meteor Shower 2026: Where to watch this meteor shower?

The meteor shower is visible from both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, including:

  • India
  • Europe
  • North America
  • Asia
  • Australia

Its radiant, the apparent point from which the meteors seem to originate, lies in the constellation Taurus. The constellation rises in the evening and climbs higher towards midnight.

Southern Taurid Meteor Shower 2026: Best viewing conditions

For the best chance of spotting meteors, observers should:

  • Choose a dark location away from city lights.
  • Watch around local midnight when the radiant is higher.
  • Allow their eyes 20–30 minutes to adjust to darkness.
  • Look across a wide area of the sky rather than directly at the radiant.
  • Check local weather forecasts for clear skies.

The Moon will be around 25% illuminated during the peak night, meaning moonlight interference is expected to be limited. No telescope or binoculars are needed. A clear, dark sky and patience are enough to watch the Southern Taurids.
